nodes.title: Revisions
nodes.body: 06-12-90. Thomas Czapla; NOAA SEA Division, Silver Spring, MD.

nodes.title: TAXONOMY
nodes.body:
Common Name: Hard Clam
Scientific Name: Mercenaria mercenaria

nodes.title: Phylum Mollusca
nodes.body:
Class: Bivalvia
      Order: Eulamellabranchia
      Family: Veneridae

Other Common Names: Quahog, hard-shelled clam, little neck, cherrystone clam, chowder clam (670). Andrews (13) gives M. campechiensis and M. campechiensis texana common names as the southern quahog and the Texas quahog respectively.

nodes.title: VALUE & STATUS
nodes.body:
Commercial:  No commercial industry has been recognized probably because of the limited numbers.
Recreational: Taken and eaten recreationally by local fishermen.
Indicator: Hard calms like most bivalves are used to study the concentrations and bioaccumulations of toxic organic chemicals and heavy metal uptake (488) due to their filter feeding abilities.

nodes.title: Mating/Spawning
nodes.body: Histological comparisons of northern and southern quahog and their hybrids revealed spawning from December to April with peaks in December and February (15 8).

nodes.title: ECOLOGICAL INTERACTIONS
nodes.body:
Predation:  Arnold (22) demonstrated the effects of predation by blue crab on different substrates, with predation rates being higher in sand and sand/mud substrates. In addition, clams greater than 40 mm SL were not consumed, even by large crabs.
Competition:  A zone of hybridization occurs in Florida between M. mercenaria and M. campechiensis (181). Dillon and ~anzi (181) recommend that the hard clams under M. campechiensis from Texas be re-grouped as mercenaria campechiensis texana, based on seven isozyme loci, six morphometric variables, shell ridging and nacre color.
